source.title: Prioritized memory access explains planning and hippocampal replay.

confidence_rationale: A normative theory, fit to rodent replay data, that derives exactly the two quantities MECH-443/MECH-444 posit: replay is ordered by UTILITY = gain x need, not uniformly. The 'gain' term is the policy-change a backup would produce -- the direct analog of value-prediction-error / staleness. High source quality (Nat Neurosci, unifies a large body of replay findings); the residual risk is that REE's rule-arbitration layer is not a tabular spatial value table, so the prioritization signal must be re-derived in REE's substrate, not transplanted.
failure_signatures: Prioritization here is over a tabular spatial value function; mapping onto REE's rule-arbitration weights assumes an analogous 'gain' (policy-change-per-update) can be computed at the rule layer, which the substrate does not yet expose.

The theory is normative/computational, not a cellular demonstration that SWR events carry a graded priority signal -- it predicts the ordering that recordings show, it does not measure a write-strength gate.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Which memories are replayed is governed by a normative priority -- the expected value of a backup, factorized as gain (how much the backup would change the policy) times need (how often the state will be visited) -- and this single rule reproduces the reward-, novelty- and goal-biases seen in hippocampal replay.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-443: the rule-write channel opened by MECH-319 should not admit replayed transitions uniformly but in priority order, weighted by an update-utility signal (gain x need). MECH-444: the 'gain' term IS a staleness/value-error measure -- a backup is high-gain precisely when the current estimate is most wrong/outdated, which motivates refreshing the write target against the current model before it updates the rule layer.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Mattar & Daw prioritize accesses to a tabular spatial value function; REE's rule-arbitration layer is a parametric EMA over rule_state, so 'gain' cannot be read off directly and must be operationalized (e.g. surprise / value-prediction-error proxy). The theory supports the EXISTENCE of a graded priority and that it tracks update-utility, not the specific REE implementation.
mapping.source_context: Computational model of nonlocal hippocampal replay in simulated spatial navigation (rat place-cell data as the comparison target).

confidence_components.notes: Weighted toward mapping_fidelity: the gain x need decomposition is an unusually clean analog of MECH-443's priority and MECH-444's staleness term, but the tabular-vs-parametric gap is real.
